chapter: Band personalities, Duke's last years and the office
title: Unpaid taxes and Tizol's unemployment claim
summary: He couldn't draw unemployment because the office had not paid in taxes or Social Security.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Juan, tell her about the time you came home for six weeks and went to draw your unemployment and couldn't get any money.
Oh, I don't want to mention that.
What? Nobody has been paying in to it?
Well, that's the reason he owed so much money to the income tax people. See, he was not paying that or the Social Security; he was not paying anything.
And they asked Juan to show them his work slips, and he came home and took his work slips, and they said, 'Well, we're sorry, but we don't have anything down here for you.'
No. I went to the union; I went through everything, and they tried to find things out and they said they can't do nothing.
Can't do anything because it hasn't
been paid in, so it can't be paid out.
Duke didn't worry about such things, but he left it to people to do for him.
He left it to the manager. And Juan had been with Duke -- my gracious -- 12 or 13 years then.
Well, who was running the office then? Mitler? When Bill Mitler was in charge of the books?
No, Bill Mitler hasn't been in charge of the books for quite a while.
It was Celley who was the manager.
